questions.question: Which statement best describes the temperature required to melt solid rock?
options: Rock melts at room temperature
Rock melts at the same temperature as ice
The melting point of rock is very high
Rock cannot melt under any conditions

questions.question: What is liquid rock called when it reaches the surface of Earth?
options: Magma
Lava
Sediment
Mantle

questions.question: Where does intrusive igneous rock form?
options: Outside Earth's crust
Inside Earth's crust
At the bottom of the ocean only
In Earth's atmosphere

questions.question: What determines the size of crystals formed in cooling melted rock?
options: The color of the molten rock
The rate at which the melted rock cools
The amount of oxygen present in the air
The depth of nearby ocean water

questions.question: Which two main arrangements can rock grains have?
options: Square or triangular
Round or interlocking
Liquid or gas
Smooth or metallic

questions.question: How are atoms arranged inside a crystal?
options: In a random, chaotic arrangement
In a very regular pattern
In loose, fluid layers
In single isolated pairs

questions.question: What combination of conditions can push particles together to form crystals in some substances?
options: Low temperature and zero pressure
Very high pressure at a high temperature
Freezing temperatures at low pressure
High humidity and cool breeze

questions.question: Why can large crystals grow inside solid rock between tectonic plates?
options: Because sunlight reaches deep into the gaps
Because pressure and temperature are high enough there
Because cold water freezes the rock rapidly
Because air pockets expand the crystals

questions.question: How do metamorphic rocks form?
options: By rapid cooling of lava on Earth's surface
Under extreme pressure and temperature altering original structures
By layers of sand being washed away by ocean waves
By evaporation of seawater in shallow lakes

questions.question: What useful physical property can aligned crystals give to certain metamorphic rocks?
options: Making them float on water
Allowing them to easily be separated into sheets
Making them completely transparent like clear glass
Giving them a soft, rubbery texture

questions.question: Which of the following defines a mineral?
options: A man-made mixture of gases
A naturally occurring pure substance with a crystal structure
Any soft organic matter found in topsoil
A liquid solution of salt and rainwater

questions.question: Which description best fits the planet Earth?
options: A flat disk made entirely of ice
A gas giant planet with a thick hydrogen crust
A spherical, rocky planet with a thin crust partially covered in water
A hollow metal sphere surrounded by dust

questions.question: What is the dense rocky layer located directly under Earth's crust called?
options: The outer core
The mantle
The inner core
The atmosphere

questions.question: What is the structure of Earth's core?
options: A liquid metallic core surrounded by a solid outer layer
A solid metallic core surrounded by a liquid outer core
A gas core surrounded by liquid rock
A solid rock core surrounded by empty space

questions.question: What happens to temperature and pressure towards the centre of Earth?
options: They decrease, making the inner core frozen solid
They stay constant throughout all layers
They increase, making the inner core extremely hot and solid
Temperature increases but pressure drops to zero

questions.question: What evidence supports the idea that Earth's continents were once all joined together?
options: Matching rock formations and fossils across different continents
Identical weather patterns on every continent today
The presence of modern cities on all landmasses
Equal amounts of rainfall recorded on every continent

questions.question: What are the large pieces of Earth's crust that move very slowly called?
options: Tectonic plates
Mantle layers
Sedimentary bands
Magma streams

questions.question: What structural feature characterizes sedimentary rocks?
options: Crystals aligned in parallel bands
Distinct grains that are stuck together
A smooth glass-like melted surface
Interlocking metallic crystals

questions.question: How do crystal arrangements differ between igneous and metamorphic rocks?
options: Igneous crystals line up; metamorphic crystals point in many directions
Igneous crystals point in many directions; metamorphic crystals mostly line up
Igneous rocks have no crystals; metamorphic rocks are purely liquid
Both rock types have crystals aligned in identical straight lines

questions.question: Which structural feature makes a rock non-porous?
options: Containing distinct rounded grains with air gaps
Containing interlocking grains or interlocking crystals
Being soft enough to crumble easily by hand
Having a high amount of trapped open pore space
